name: WISE 0855−0714
description: Official test target. Coldest known brown dwarf, ~2.3 pc away, ~8.2"/yr. Extremely red (J=25, W2=13.7): SPHEREx sees it only at 3.8–5.0 µm (D5–D6), faint in single exposures. Only DR1 data so far: ~1.4 SPHEREx pixels of motion.

notes: Automatic detection and catalog matching were not run.

Pixel values and stretch limits are IMAGE - ZODI (SPHEREx zodiacal model subtracted) in MJy/sr; PNGs use an asinh mapping with the same contrast for every frame of a detector, and transparent pixels mean no data. Saturated star cores that SPHEREx left empty (NaN) and detector-defect pixels (NONFUNC, HOT, COLD, PERSIST, SNOWBALL, and SUR_ERROR that is not part of a star's profile, e.g. cosmic-ray hits) are filled from their neighbours for display only; SUR_ERROR pixels on a star and finite OVERFLOW pixels are shown as recorded. All of them count as invalid in valid_fraction. thumb.png is a D1 frame.

Frame selection: downloaded 80 candidate frame(s) (up to 2 x max_frames=40) and kept 40, spread round-robin over seasons x detectors; inside each (season, detector) the frames whose wavelength at the field centre is closest to a per-detector reference (D1 0.842 um, D2 1.552 um, D3 2.258 um, D4 2.777 um, D5 4.074 um, D6 4.895 um) come first, then those nearest the season middle; frames without a known wavelength rank last. Rejected 1 bad frame(s) whose IMAGE - ZODI robust scatter exceeds 15x the noise of their VARIANCE plane (background steps). Downloaded 24 more D2/D3 frame(s) only to find J/H/Ks wavelengths for the false-color composites; they are not blink frames.

Registration check: every frame's field stars were compared with their median position over the field's candidate frames (all detectors: a correct WCS puts a star at the same grid position at every wavelength); 79 of 79 blink candidate frame(s) and 24 of 24 J/H/Ks top-up frame(s) checked (kept: median 0.03 px, max 0.33 px).

False-color composites: 3 'detectors' and 3 'jhk' season composite(s) (infrared, not true color). detectors = full range: blue = D1 (fallback D2), green = D3 (D4), red = D6 (D5), coadds of the season's published frames. jhk = 2MASS-like: blue / green / red = coadd of the season's downloaded exposures (including unpublished candidates) within 0.06 um of J 1.25 / H 1.65 / Ks 2.17 um at the field centre, else the nearest one within 0.12 um. Each channel: one weight per frame, sky removed, bad pixels left out; a pixel bad in every frame of a channel (saturated core, detector defect, ramp-fit error) is drawn neutral at the brightest channel's level, so saturated cores look white (display only). Green spans 2 sigma below the sky to the bright end of its usable pixels; red and blue are scaled to green by the median field-star flux ratio (target halo excluded), so typical field stars look white; limits shared by every season with the same detectors; colour-preserving asinh (Lupton et al. 2004).
Skipped 1 frame(s): 2025W19_1B_0241_4D1: bad frame: noise 19.6x VARIANCE

Full range: red = D6 4.91 um, green = D3 2.29 um, blue = D1 1.02 um (mean wavelength at the field centre).
Colour balance: red and blue scaled to green by the median flux ratio of the field stars (red x0.276, blue x0.903; median of 3 season fit(s)), so typical field stars look white.
The red channel (D6) is noisy here (pixel noise 10% of its range): isolated red specks are mostly noise, not red objects.
Colours are relative to the field: typical field stars look roughly white and an object redder than they are looks red.
